title: PhysxMaterialAPI
summary: PhysX tuning for a physics material: combine modes and compliant contact. Read only when the prim also carries PhysicsMaterialAPI (that API is what enumerates materials) and only when PhysxMaterialAPI is listed in usd-schemas.
producer_scope: Every declared attribute is published at its resolved value. Token attributes are published as token-id columns (TOKEN_ID semantic); the consumer reads them as token ids. Nothing is rewritten or created by the producer.

columns.name: physxMaterial:frictionCombineMode
columns.absent: average. Accepted tokens: average, min, max, multiply. An unrecognised token or an invalid token id silently resolves to average.
columns.notes: PhysX: the material's friction combine mode, PxCombineMode eAVERAGE=0 eMIN=1 eMULTIPLY=2 eMAX=3; the runtime's own combine-mode enum has the same ordinals and is cast directly. No verify block: the generator turns a sample into a numeric C++ literal and cannot express a token string, and a token-id sample would not be portable across stages.

columns.name: physxMaterial:restitutionCombineMode
columns.absent: average. Same tokens and unrecognised-token rule as physxMaterial:frictionCombineMode.
columns.notes: PhysX: the material's restitution combine mode. No verify block, see physxMaterial:frictionCombineMode.

columns.name: physxMaterial:dampingCombineMode
columns.absent: average. Same tokens and unrecognised-token rule as physxMaterial:frictionCombineMode.
columns.notes: PhysX: the material's damping combine mode. No verify block, see physxMaterial:frictionCombineMode.

columns.name: physxMaterial:compliantContactAccelerationSpring

verify.notes: The flag is set regardless of stiffness; PhysX ignores it while restitution is non-negative.

columns.absent: Off: compliant stiffness and damping are force-based. On, they are interpreted as accelerations.

columns.name: physxMaterial:compliantContactStiffness

verify.notes: No sample: a positive stiffness is stored as a negative restitution and would invalidate the physics:restitution check on the same material. The absent check still holds (0 means the restitution is left as authored).

columns.absent: 0.0: compliant contact off; physics:restitution reaches PhysX unchanged. Any positive value switches the material to compliant contact by storing -stiffness as the PhysX restitution.
columns.units: force/length (acceleration/length when the acceleration spring flag is set)
columns.notes: Lower-clamped to 0 on read (a negative value becomes 0, i.e. off); no upper bound.

columns.name: physxMaterial:compliantContactDamping

verify.notes: No sample: a non-zero damping is only meaningful with a positive compliant stiffness, which the restitution check forbids in the same test. The absent check holds.

columns.units: force*s/length (acceleration*s/length when the acceleration spring flag is set)
columns.notes: Lower-clamped to 0 on read. The consumer always sets the damping on the PhysX material so that PhysX reports damping-without-stiffness itself.

interactions.rule: physics:restitution and compliantContactStiffness share one PhysX slot: stiffness > 0 replaces the restitution with -stiffness. The scene default material never receives the compliant-contact fields, only the three combine modes.

notes: physxMaterial:improvePatchFriction is neither in the current PhysxMaterialAPI schema fallback inventory nor read anywhere by the consumer; it is not a column of this contract.

The runtime's own combine-mode enum (average=0, min, multiply, max) matches PxCombineMode ordinal for ordinal; token order in the schema (average, min, max, multiply) differs from the enum order, which only matters if a future contract maps tokens to integers.
